answer: Sybil resistance via congestion-priced identity escrow: each new account locks a refundable bond priced by auction over the pending registration queue. Flooding the queue raises the clearing price like a rising tide, so every extra fake identity costs the attacker more than the last, while honest arrivals at anchor windows of low demand pay almost nothing. Bonds mature only after the account earns genuine attestations; collusion forfeits them to a pool funding nectar-style rewards for honest users. Attack cost self-scales upward, so mass registration turns revenue-negative.
